requirements.text: The warehouse must record every vendor, a company from which goods are purchased.
A vendor is identified in business terms by its vendor account number, the identification number used by purchasing staff and in vendor correspondence.
The warehouse must retain the internal business entity identifier of each vendor in addition to the vendor account number, since other purchasing records point to the internal identifier.
The vendor's company name must be recorded and reportable.
Each vendor carries a credit rating on a five-point scale: Superior, Excellent, Above average, Average, Below average.
Reporting must present the vendor credit rating in its business wording, not as a bare code.
Each vendor carries a preferred vendor status, which is either 'preferred over other vendors supplying the same product' or 'do not use if another vendor is available'.
Purchasing management must be able to see whether orders are in fact being placed with preferred vendors.
Each vendor carries an active flag indicating whether the vendor is still actively used or is no longer used.
Vendors that are no longer used must remain in the warehouse so that historical orders placed with them stay reportable.
Where a vendor offers an electronic purchasing interface, the purchasing web service address must be recorded.
The purchasing web service address is not always populated, and reporting must tolerate its absence.

The warehouse must retain the history of changes to vendor attributes, in particular credit rating, preferred status and active flag, so that the state of a vendor at the time an order was placed can be reconstructed.
The warehouse must record, for each combination of product and vendor, the standing commercial terms under which the product is bought from that vendor.
The same product may be supplied by several vendors, and a vendor may supply several products.
The supply relationship is identified in business terms by the pairing of the product and the vendor.
The average lead time, the average span of time in days between placing an order with the vendor and receiving the purchased product, must be recorded for each product and vendor.
The standard price, the vendor's usual selling price for the product, must be recorded.
The last receipt cost, the selling price when the product was last purchased from the vendor, must be recorded.
The last receipt date, the date the product was last received from the vendor, must be recorded.
The agreed minimum and maximum order quantities for the product from the vendor must be recorded so that buyers and reporting can see whether orders respect the agreed bounds.

Which source field carries the minimum versus maximum order quantity meaning must be confirmed with the purchasing team before either is used in reporting or threshold checks, because the source field descriptions are transposed.
The quantity currently on order for the product from the vendor must be available as an indicator of open commitment.
The unit of measure in which the product is bought from the vendor must be recorded.
Quantities and prices must always be interpreted together with the unit of measure, since the same product may be bought in different units from different vendors.
The warehouse must retain the history of supply term changes (price, lead time, quantity bounds) so that trends in agreed price and lead time per vendor and product can be analysed.
Reporting must be clear about whether it shows the current value or the value as at a point in time for the running values quantity on order and last receipt figures.
The warehouse must be able to identify each purchased product consistently and join purchasing activity to the wider product information maintained outside the purchasing area.
The warehouse must record every purchase order placed with a vendor.
A purchase order is identified in business terms by its purchase order number.
Each purchase order is placed with exactly one vendor.
Each purchase order is created by one employee, the buyer who raised it.
The warehouse must be able to report purchasing activity by the employee who created the order.
Employee name, department and role must come from the HR/employee area if the business wants to report on them, since only the identity of the creating employee is available in the purchasing area.
Each purchase order names a shipping method, the shipping company and rate agreement used to bring the goods.
Each purchase order carries an order date, the date the order was created.
Each purchase order carries an estimated shipment date, the date the vendor is expected to ship.
The business must be able to compare the estimated shipment date against actual receipt activity.
requirements.obj: estimated shipment date against actual receipt

requirements.text: Each purchase order carries a status that is one of Pending, Approved, Rejected or Complete.
Reporting must present purchase order status in business wording.
The business must be able to see the population of orders in each status, in particular orders that are approved but not yet complete.
Each purchase order carries a revision number, an incrementing counter tracking how the order has changed over time.
The business must be able to know whether an order was revised and how many times.
The warehouse must retain the history of a purchase order as it changes, including status transitions and revisions, so that they are traceable over time and not overwritten by the latest state.
The business must be able to answer when an order was approved and how long it sat pending.
requirements.obj: order approval time and pending duration

requirements.text: The business expectation on revision history reconstruction must be agreed, because the source holds only the current order version with revision number and last-updated date, and reconstruction depends on source capture frequency.
Each purchase order carries financial totals: a subtotal (the sum of the value of its lines), a tax amount, a freight amount, and a total due to the vendor (subtotal plus tax plus freight).
The business must be able to analyse purchasing spend by vendor, by employee, by shipping method, and over time, using order totals.
The warehouse must be able to demonstrate that reported order totals are consistent with the underlying order lines.
Any discrepancy between the stated order total and the sum of its lines must be visible to the business as a finding.
Freight and tax are order-level charges and are not attributed to individual products in the source.
If the business wants product-level landed cost, the business must decide the basis for allocating freight and tax across order lines, since it cannot be derived from the source.
Each purchase order contains one or more lines, one per purchased product.
A purchase order line is identified in business terms by the purchase order it belongs to together with its line number.
Each purchase order line refers to exactly one product.
Each purchase order line carries the quantity ordered.
Each purchase order line carries the unit price, which is the vendor's selling price for a single unit of the product on this order.
Each purchase order line carries a line total, which is the ordered quantity multiplied by the unit price.
Each purchase order line carries a due date, the date on which the product is expected to be received.
Delivery-performance analysis must work at line level, not only at order level, because the due date is held per line and different products on the same order may be expected at different times.
The business must be able to compare the unit price actually paid on a line with the standard price agreed for that product and vendor, to identify off-contract purchasing.
requirements.obj: unit price paid with standard price agreed

requirements.text: Each purchase order line records the quantity actually received from the vendor.
Each purchase order line records the quantity rejected during inspection.
Each purchase order line records the quantity accepted into inventory, being the received quantity less the rejected quantity.
The business must be able to measure the fulfilment gap between ordered and received quantity, including under-delivery and over-delivery, per line, per order, per product and per vendor.
The business must be able to measure inspection reject rates, being rejected quantity as a share of received quantity, by vendor and by product, as the primary indicator of incoming quality.

The warehouse must retain the progression of received and rejected quantities per line over the life of the order, so that the quantity received as at a given date can be answered and partial deliveries are visible.
requirements.obj: progression of received and rejected quantities

requirements.text: The source records only cumulative received, rejected and accepted quantities per line with a last-updated date, and does not record individual receipt events, receipt dates or inspection outcomes per delivery; analysis of individual deliveries requires another source or the requirement being dropped.
The business must be able to compare the due date on a line against evidence of actual receipt, in order to measure on-time delivery by vendor.
requirements.obj: line due date with actual receipt

requirements.text: The practical measure of actual receipt timing currently available is the last receipt date held on the vendor-product supply relationship, and its sufficiency as a basis for an on-time-delivery metric must be agreed with the business.

The business must be able to compare actual elapsed time from order to receipt against the average lead time recorded for that vendor and product, to validate whether recorded lead times are realistic.
requirements.obj: actual elapsed time with average lead time

requirements.text: The warehouse must record every shipping method available for inbound purchases.
A shipping method is identified in business terms by the shipping company name.
A shipping method has an internal shipping method identifier that is used on purchase orders.
Each shipping method carries a minimum shipping charge (ship base).
Each shipping method carries a charge per pound (ship rate).
The business must be able to analyse freight cost by shipping method.
The business must be able to compare the freight actually charged on orders against the base and per-pound rates agreed with the shipping company.
requirements.obj: freight charged with agreed shipping rates

requirements.text: The warehouse must retain the history of ship base and ship rate so that freight charged on a historical order can be assessed against the rates in force at that time.
requirements.obj: history of ship base and ship rate

requirements.text: The technical replication identifier on shipping method records in the source has no business meaning and is not required for reporting.
A vendor supplies one or more products, and a product may be supplied by more than one vendor.
Each vendor-product supply relationship carries its own agreed price, lead time and order quantity bounds.
A purchase order is placed with exactly one vendor.
A purchase order is created by one employee.
A purchase order specifies one shipping method.
Receipt and inspection outcomes attach to the purchase order line, not to the order as a whole.
Products on order lines are normally, but not necessarily, products for which a supply relationship with that vendor exists.
Where a line names a product with no recorded supply relationship for that vendor, the warehouse must surface this as a finding rather than hide it as a data error.
requirements.obj: line with product lacking vendor supply relationship

requirements.text: The warehouse must use the last-modified date and time carried by every record in the purchasing source to establish when information changed.
The warehouse must not present a value as current when a more recent change exists.

All monetary amounts in purchasing are held in a single currency in the source with no currency indicator; if vendors in other currencies are used, the currency of purchase orders and prices must be clarified as it cannot be established from the schema.
Coded values with defined business meanings, namely purchase order status, vendor credit rating, preferred vendor status and active flag, must be presented in reporting in their business wording.
The mapping of codes to business wording must be held once and applied consistently.
Quantities must always be interpreted together with the unit of measure recorded on the relevant vendor-product supply relationship.
Reporting must prevent aggregation of quantities across products or units of measure without regard to the unit.
requirements.obj: aggregation of quantities across units of measure

requirements.text: Records that no longer represent current operational reality, such as inactive vendors, completed or rejected orders and discontinued supply relationships, must be retained in full.
Nothing may be physically removed because it has ceased to be current.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-002 explicitly states a vendor is identified in business terms by its vendor account number, used by purchasing staff and in correspondence; it is business-recognised, unique and non-null (REQ-001).

REQ-003 requires retaining it because other purchasing records (e.g., purchase orders, REQ-031) reference it, but it is an internal/system identifier, so it is a weaker business key than the account number; keep as a secondary reference.

REQ-028 requires consistent identification of each purchased product and joining to product information outside purchasing; REQ-003-2 shows lines refer to a product. ProductID is the only known product identifier in source, though the requirements do not explicitly call it unique.
REQ-030 states a purchase order is identified in business terms by its purchase order number; it is stable, unique and non-null, and is the key referenced by order lines (REQ-002-2).

business_keys.field: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID (purchase order and line number)
business_keys.rationale: REQ-002-2 states a line is identified by the purchase order it belongs to together with its line number; composite key combining the parent order key and line identifier.
REQ-021-2 states a shipping method is identified in business terms by the shipping company name; business-recognised and used to identify the method.
REQ-022-2 notes this internal identifier is used on purchase orders (REQ-033-2), but it is system-assigned and thus a weak business key; needed for referential joins only.
REQ-016 states the supply relationship is identified by the pairing of product and vendor (also REQ-014, REQ-029-2); composite of the product and vendor business keys.

REQ-032 and REQ-034 state each order is created by one employee and only the identity of the employee is available in purchasing; EmployeeID is the source reference, but employee master data comes from the HR area and no explicit business identifier is stated.

hubs.description: Second level of the product classification hierarchy.

hubs.name: hub_product_model

hubs.name: hub_culture

hubs.name: hub_unit_measure

hubs.name: hub_product_description
hubs.description: Library entry of a free-text marketing description.

hubs.name: hub_product_photo
hubs.description: Library entry of a product photograph.

hubs.name: hub_illustration
hubs.description: Technical diagram used in manufacturing instructions.

hubs.name: hub_document
hubs.description: Entry (folder or document) in the controlled document library, identified by its hierarchy node.

hubs.name: hub_location

hubs.name: hub_work_order
hubs.description: Work order raised to manufacture a product.

hubs.name: hub_product_review
hubs.description: Customer-submitted product review.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order
hubs.description: Purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order_detail
hubs.description: Purchase order line, identified by the purchase order plus its line number.

hubs.name: hub_ship_method

links.name: link_address_state_province
links.description: The state or province in which an address sits; country is derived via the state.

links.name: link_state_province_country_region
links.description: Each state or province belongs to exactly one country or region.

links.name: link_business_entity_address

links.name: link_business_entity_contact

links.name: link_business_entity_department_shift
links.description: Employee assignment to a department and shift over time, from EmployeeDepartmentHistory. The employee has one current assignment at a time, so the employee is the driving key.

links.name: link_job_candidate_business_entity
links.description: Links a job candidate record to the employee hired from it. If a link exists, the candidate was hired.
links.unit_of_work: JobCandidateID + BusinessEntityID: a candidate hired as an employee

links.name: link_product_subcategory
links.description: Product placed in (at most one) subcategory.

links.name: link_product_subcategory_category
links.description: Subcategory belongs to exactly one category.

links.name: link_product_model

links.name: link_product_unit_measure
links.description: Units of measure in which a product's size and weight are expressed.

links.name: link_product_model_description_culture

links.name: link_product_model_illustration

links.name: link_product_product_photo
links.description: Photographs used for products (many-to-many).

links.name: link_product_document
links.description: Documents applying to products (many-to-many).

links.name: link_document_business_entity
links.description: Document owner (employee, sourced from Document.Owner) joined to the existing HR business entity hub.

links.name: link_bill_of_materials
links.description: Component-in-assembly relationship between two products, with the unit of the component quantity.

links.name: link_product_location
links.description: Inventory holding of a product at a location.

links.name: link_work_order_product
links.description: Product being made by a work order.

links.name: link_work_order_scrap_reason
links.description: Scrap reason recorded on a work order (optional).

links.name: link_work_order_routing
links.description: Operation of a work order, the product manufactured and the location where it is performed.

links.name: link_inventory_transaction_product
links.description: Product involved in an inventory transaction.

links.name: link_product_review_product
links.description: Product a review relates to.

links.name: link_product_vendor
links.description: Vendor-product supply relationship: which vendor supplies which product, and the unit of measure it is bought in. Many-to-many.
links.unit_of_work: ProductID + vendor BusinessEntityID (with the UnitMeasureCode the product is bought in)

links.name: link_purchase_order
links.description: Purchase order header: the vendor the order is placed with, the employee who created it, and the shipping method it names.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID with VendorID, EmployeeID and ShipMethodID from one order header

links.name: link_purchase_order_detail
links.description: Purchase order line: the order it belongs to and the product it refers to.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID with the line's ProductID

links.name: link_purchase_order_detail_product
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderDetail.ProductID references PRODUCTID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

links.name: link_purchase_order_business_entity
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_details

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_name

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_type

satellites.split_rationale: Classification used for wide aggregated reporting; changes at a different rate from names.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_consent

satellites.split_rationale: Compliance-sensitive consent tracked independently of name changes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_sensitive

satellites.split_rationale: Data classification: sensitive personal data restricted separately; XML data type.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_email
satellites.description: A person's email addresses, numbered within the person, with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source relation at finer grain (several per person).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_phone
satellites.description: A person's telephone numbers qualified by phone number type, with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source relation at finer grain (several per person).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_credential
satellites.description: Existence and last-change date of a sign-in credential only; hash and salt are never loaded.

satellites.name: sat_address_details
satellites.description: Street, city and postal details of an address with full history.

satellites.name: sat_address_location
satellites.description: Geographic coordinates of an address for mapping and territory analysis.

satellites.name: sat_address_type_details
satellites.description: Address type descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_contact_type_details
satellites.description: Contact type descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_phone_number_type_details
satellites.description: Phone number type name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_details
satellites.description: Country or region name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_details
satellites.description: State or province ISO code, no-genuine-code flag and name.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of the party-address relationship.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_details
satellites.description: Employee attributes that can be widely reported: network login, job title, hire date, salaried/hourly flag, active flag and last-updated timestamp. History is kept because the source overwrites these values.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_leave

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy
satellites.description: The employee's position and level in the corporate hierarchy. Changes are captured because the source holds only the current position.
satellites.split_rationale: Hierarchy position changes independently of other attributes and supports reconstructing past structures

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_pay
satellites.description: Employee pay rate history: one row per effective rate-change date, with the hourly rate and pay frequency.

satellites.name: sat_department_details
satellites.description: Department name, group membership and last-changed date, with history kept for as-was reporting.

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift definition (name, start and end time), with history kept so past shift hours stay understandable.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_resume
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé as a structured document, plus its last-updated timestamp.

satellites.description: Last-updated timestamp of each assignment record, one row per assignment start date, used to spot stale records.

satellites.name: sat_product_list_price_history
satellites.description: List price periods per product.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source at finer grain (product + start date).

satellites.description: Category name.

satellites.description: Subcategory name.

contracts.name: ProductVendor
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset linking each product to the vendor that supplies it, with purchasing terms (lead time, pricing, order quantity limits) and last receipt details. schema.name: ProductID
schema.description: Identifier of the product supplied by the vendor. Part of the business key; references the product.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the vendor (business entity) supplying the product. Part of the business key; references the vendor.

schema.name: AverageLeadTime
schema.description: Average time between placing a purchase order and receiving the product from the vendor (unit not stated in requirements, typically days).

schema.name: StandardPrice
schema.description: Vendor's usual selling price for the product.

schema.name: LastReceiptCost
schema.description: Unit cost paid the last time the product was received from the vendor.

schema.name: LastReceiptDate
schema.description: Date the product was last received from the vendor.

schema.name: MinOrderQty
schema.description: Minimum quantity that can be ordered from the vendor for this product.

schema.name: MaxOrderQty
schema.description: Maximum quantity that can be ordered from the vendor for this product.

schema.name: OnOrderQty
schema.description: Quantity currently on order with the vendor for this product.

schema.name: UnitMeasureCode
schema.description: Code of the unit of measure used for the product's quantities with this vendor.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: PurchaseOrderDetail
contracts.doc: Line-item detail of a purchase order, one row per product ordered on a purchase order, sourced from the PurchaseOrderDetail source table and staged for the vault. The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key integrity (PurchaseOrderID, PurchaseOrderDetailID). Ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human review checkpoint.

schema.name: PurchaseOrderID
schema.description: Identifier of the purchase order (header) this line item belongs to.

schema.name: PurchaseOrderDetailID
schema.description: Identifier of the individual line item within the purchase order detail.

schema.name: DueDate
schema.description: Date the ordered product is expected to be delivered.

schema.name: OrderQty
schema.description: Quantity of the product ordered on this line.

schema.name: ProductID
schema.description: Identifier of the product ordered on this line.

schema.name: UnitPrice
schema.description: Price per unit of the product ordered.

schema.name: LineTotal
schema.description: Per-line purchase amount (order quantity multiplied by unit price).

schema.name: ReceivedQty
schema.description: Quantity actually received from the vendor for this line.

schema.name: RejectedQty
schema.description: Quantity rejected during inspection for this line.

schema.name: StockedQty
schema.description: Quantity accepted and placed into stock for this line.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: PurchaseOrderHeader
contracts.doc: Purchase order header records from the source system, one row per purchase order, covering the ordering employee, vendor, ship method, order and ship dates, and monetary totals. The contract enforces the declared schema, business key (PurchaseOrderID) and not-null rules; value-level semantics are advisory pending producer/consumer review.

schema.name: PurchaseOrderID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the purchase order (business key).

schema.name: RevisionNumber
schema.description: Revision number of the purchase order, incremented when the order is changed.

schema.name: Status
schema.description: Current status code of the purchase order. The allowed value set is not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: EmployeeID
schema.description: Identifier of the employee who created the purchase order.

schema.name: VendorID
schema.description: Identifier of the vendor the order is placed with (corresponds to Vendor.BusinessEntityID).

schema.name: ShipMethodID
schema.description: Identifier of the shipping method used (corresponds to ShipMethod.ShipMethodID).

schema.name: OrderDate
schema.description: Date the purchase order was created.

schema.name: ShipDate
schema.description: Expected or actual ship date for the order; may be absent until shipped.

schema.name: SubTotal
schema.description: Order subtotal, before tax and freight.

schema.name: TaxAmt
schema.description: Tax amount on the purchase order.

schema.name: Freight
schema.description: Shipping cost for the purchase order.

schema.name: TotalDue
schema.description: Total amount due to the vendor, including tax and freight.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: ShipMethod
contracts.doc: Shipping method reference data (carriers/delivery options) used by purchase orders, staged from the ShipMethod source table. The contract enforces the declared schema, business key (ShipMethodID) uniqueness and not-null rules; ownership and agreement are pending human review.

schema.name: ShipMethodID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the shipping method; business key referenced by purchase order headers.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the shipping method.

schema.name: ShipBase
schema.description: Minimum shipping charge for the method.

schema.name: ShipRate
schema.description: Shipping charge per unit of measure (e.g. per weight) for the method.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique row identifier (GUID) for the source record.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: Vendor
contracts.doc: Vendor represents a supplier from which the organization purchases goods, as staged from the source Vendor table. The contract enforces the declared schema, business key (BusinessEntityID) uniqueness and not-null checks; ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human review checkpoint.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the vendor business entity; business key of the vendor.

schema.name: AccountNumber
schema.description: Vendor account number used to identify the vendor in purchasing.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the vendor company.

schema.name: CreditRating
schema.description: Credit rating assigned to the vendor. Allowed value set and meaning not stated in the requirements.

schema.name: PreferredVendorStatus
schema.description: Indicates whether the vendor is a preferred vendor for purchasing.

schema.name: ActiveFlag
schema.description: Indicates whether the vendor record is currently active.

schema.name: PurchasingWebServiceURL
schema.description: URL of the vendor's purchasing web service.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the vendor record was last modified in the source.

# ADR-0001: Data Vault model derived from requirements

**Status:** Proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Decision makers:** Vault-Agent (generated) — pending human review

## Context

This model was derived automatically by the Vault-Agent pipeline from 97 requirement(s) and 9 business key candidate(s). It records the Data Vault 2.0 structures the modeler chose and traces each back to the requirements that justify it.

## Decision

Model the following Data Vault 2.0 structures.

### Hubs (3)

- **hub_purchase_order** — business key `PurchaseOrderID`. Purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number. _(requirements: REQ-029, REQ-030, REQ-044, REQ-044-2)_
- **hub_purchase_order_detail** — business key `purchase_order_line`. Purchase order line, identified by the purchase order plus its line number. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-002-2, REQ-034-2, REQ-008-2)_
- **hub_ship_method** — business key `ShipMethodID`. Shipping method for inbound purchases. Keyed on ShipMethodID, the identifier purchase orders reference (REQ-022-2), so orders can join to it. The shipping company name is kept in a satellite. _(requirements: REQ-020-2, REQ-021-2, REQ-022-2, REQ-035, REQ-033-2)_

### Links (5)

- **link_product_vendor** — connects hub_product, hub_business_entity, hub_unit_measure. Vendor-product supply relationship: which vendor supplies which product, and the unit of measure it is bought in. Many-to-many. Unit of work: ProductID + vendor BusinessEntityID (with the UnitMeasureCode the product is bought in). _(requirements: REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-024, REQ-025, REQ-028, REQ-029-2, REQ-030-2, REQ-042-2)_
- **link_purchase_order** — connects hub_purchase_order, hub_business_entity (vendor), hub_business_entity (employee), hub_ship_method. Purchase order header: the vendor the order is placed with, the employee who created it, and the shipping method it names. Unit of work: PurchaseOrderID with VendorID, EmployeeID and ShipMethodID from one order header. _(requirements: REQ-031, REQ-032, REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-035, REQ-048, REQ-008, REQ-031-2, REQ-032-2, REQ-033-2)_
- **link_purchase_order_detail** — connects hub_purchase_order_detail, hub_purchase_order, hub_product. Purchase order line: the order it belongs to and the product it refers to. Unit of work: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID with the line's ProductID. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-002-2, REQ-003-2, REQ-028, REQ-035-2, REQ-036-2, REQ-049)_
- **link_purchase_order_detail_product** — connects hub_purchase_order_detail, hub_product. Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderDetail.ProductID references PRODUCTID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34). _(requirements: —)_
- **link_purchase_order_business_entity** — connects hub_purchase_order, hub_business_entity. Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34). _(requirements: —)_

### Satellites (10)

- **sat_business_entity_vendor_details** — on hub_business_entity; payload: AccountNumber, Name, PurchasingWebServiceURL. Vendor identifying and descriptive attributes: account number, company name and purchasing web service address (may be empty). Source table: Vendor. Split rationale: Slowly changing descriptive attributes, kept apart from the classification codes that change more often.. _(requirements: REQ-002, REQ-004, REQ-011, REQ-012)_
- **sat_business_entity_vendor_status** — on hub_business_entity; payload: CreditRating, PreferredVendorStatus, ActiveFlag, ModifiedDate. Vendor credit rating, preferred status and active flag, with history so a vendor's state when an order was placed can be rebuilt. Source table: Vendor. Split rationale: Coded classification attributes whose history is explicitly required; they change at a different rate from the name and account details.. _(requirements: REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-013, REQ-037-2, REQ-040-2)_
- **sat_product_vendor_terms** — on link_product_vendor; payload: AverageLeadTime, StandardPrice, MinOrderQty, MaxOrderQty, ModifiedDate. Agreed supply terms: average lead time, standard price, and minimum/maximum order quantities (the min/max meaning must be confirmed, REQ-022). History is kept for trend analysis. Source table: ProductVendor. Split rationale: Negotiated terms that change rarely, kept apart from the running receipt and on-order figures.. _(requirements: REQ-017, REQ-018, REQ-021, REQ-022, REQ-026, REQ-030-2, REQ-009-2, REQ-019-2, REQ-037-2)_
- **sat_product_vendor_receipt** — on link_product_vendor; payload: LastReceiptCost, LastReceiptDate, OnOrderQty. Running operational figures: last receipt cost, last receipt date and quantity currently on order. Source table: ProductVendor. Split rationale: Fast-changing running values, separated from the agreed terms by rate of change.. _(requirements: REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-023, REQ-027, REQ-018-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_details** — on hub_purchase_order; payload: RevisionNumber, Status, OrderDate, ShipDate, ModifiedDate. Order status, revision number, order date and estimated ship date, with history of status changes and revisions. Source table: PurchaseOrderHeader. Split rationale: Lifecycle and status attributes, kept apart from the financial totals.. _(requirements: REQ-036, REQ-037, REQ-038, REQ-039, REQ-040, REQ-041, REQ-042, REQ-043, REQ-044, REQ-045, REQ-046, REQ-037-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_totals** — on hub_purchase_order; payload: SubTotal, TaxAmt, Freight, TotalDue. Order-level financial totals: subtotal, tax, freight and total due. Source table: PurchaseOrderHeader. Split rationale: Monetary amounts, split from the status attributes by data type.. _(requirements: REQ-047, REQ-048, REQ-049, REQ-050, REQ-051, REQ-052, REQ-025-2, REQ-026-2, REQ-039-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_detail_order** — on hub_purchase_order_detail; payload: OrderQty, UnitPrice, LineTotal, DueDate, ModifiedDate. Ordered terms on each line: quantity ordered, unit price, line total and due date. Source table: PurchaseOrderDetail. Split rationale: Values set when the order is placed, which rarely change afterwards.. _(requirements: REQ-004-2, REQ-005-2, REQ-006-2, REQ-007-2, REQ-008-2, REQ-009-2, REQ-017-2, REQ-037-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_detail_receipt** — on hub_purchase_order_detail; payload: ReceivedQty, RejectedQty, StockedQty. Cumulative received, rejected and accepted quantities on each line. History shows how they progress, including partial deliveries. Source table: PurchaseOrderDetail. Split rationale: Receipt and inspection progress changes over the life of the order, separately from the ordered terms.. _(requirements: REQ-010-2, REQ-011-2, REQ-012-2, REQ-013-2, REQ-014-2, REQ-015-2, REQ-016-2, REQ-034-2)_
- **sat_ship_method_details** — on hub_ship_method; payload: Name. Shipping company name (the business identifier). The rowguid replication column is left out because it has no business meaning. Source table: ShipMethod. Split rationale: Stable descriptive name, kept apart from the rates.. _(requirements: REQ-021-2, REQ-028-2)_
- **sat_ship_method_rates** — on hub_ship_method; payload: ShipBase, ShipRate, ModifiedDate. Ship base (minimum charge) and ship rate (charge per pound), with history so historical freight can be checked against the rates in force at the time. Source table: ShipMethod. Split rationale: Commercial rates with required history, which change at a different rate from the name.. _(requirements: REQ-023-2, REQ-024-2, REQ-025-2, REQ-026-2, REQ-027-2, REQ-037-2)_
